identity.notes: Root of the graph, deliberately. The ban anchor outlives every other record (docs/01 §Account deletion). Session protocol is in docs/04 §Auth.

profile.notes: Calls content because an interest id arriving from a client is untrusted input: "the client got the list from us" is not validation. Calls media to verify a representation is owned, ready and past moderation. Calls safety because a nickname, bio or prompt answer is classified at save time — a profile is a broadcast surface, and a slur in a bio reaches more people than one in a message (docs/06 §Layer 2).

discovery.notes:
Calls exactly one module, and only at request time: a bulk eligibility filter. Everything else arrives as events into its projection.
This split is the point. Being allowed to consume profile's events is not permission to call ProfileApi per card — that would be an N+1 across a module boundary on the product's main surface.
Hard exclusions are never eventual. A block, a ban or a cooldown arriving three seconds late would put an excluded profile back in the feed, which would put eventual consistency inside a product invariant. So the projection carries ranking material — proximity, freshness, fatigue, boost state, capacity pressure — and `safety.api.filterEligible(viewer, candidateIds)` is called once, synchronously, with the whole candidate batch before ranking. One call, authoritative, not fifty.
Two different policies, deliberately separate API methods: `filterDiscoverable(viewer, ids)` applies only HARD VISIBILITY exclusions — block, ban, account state, hard cooldown. `contactPolicy(sender, receiver)` answers the composer-time question — door mode, effort floor, inbound capacity, contact restrictions.
Being visible and being writable-to are not the same thing. A receiver who requires a profile must still appear in Discover; that setting decides the identity state of a request, not whether they exist. Collapsing the two would let a future change quietly remove people from the feed for having adjusted a preference.
The visibility call is authoritative to the bottom: safety asks identity for the active set in the same batch, so a deleted, banned or deactivated account is excluded even if the projection has not caught up. Otherwise a person deleted half a second ago is still a candidate, and the one guarantee that must never be eventual would be exactly as eventual as the projection.

messaging.notes:
Calls commerce because it is the only module that can compose the effective ceiling. Safety must not see who paid, so safety returns a safety cap and commerce returns a plan allowance, and messaging takes the minimum (docs/06 §Quotas). Neither module alone can compute it, and that is deliberate.
Calls profile and quiz to resolve an anchor. A client sends a reference; messaging verifies it exists and belongs to the receiver, then stores a SNAPSHOT — if the receiver edits that prompt tomorrow, a request from three months ago must still say what it was written from.
On AccountDeleted it severs identity linkage rather than deleting delivered messages (docs/01 §Account deletion).

safety.notes:
Exposes two distinct questions rather than one blurred one: `filterDiscoverable` (hard visibility: block, ban, account state, hard cooldown) and `contactPolicy` (door mode, effort floor, capacity, contact restrictions). Projections may be stale; neither of these may be.
Owns admission capacity authoritatively. "Can this person accept another request right now?" is a contact-authorisation question, not a ranking question — so it is answered here, synchronously, at request creation. Discovery consumes capacity *pressure* as a ranking input and lowers exposure; it never decides admission.
Does not depend on commerce and never learns who paid, which is what makes "money never relaxes a safety restriction" structural rather than remembered.

content.notes: Ranking weights are NOT content. Content carries text and the weights a quiz answer contributes to a trait; discovery's ranking weights are behaviour and live in remote configuration owned by discovery.

media.notes: On AccountDeleted, stored objects are deleted, not merely unlinked.

notification.notes: Subscribes and is never called. Nothing waits on a push being sent.

telemetry.notes: typed analytics; the vendor SDK exists only here

realtime_client.notes: socket envelope, dedupe, reconnect, HTTP reconciliation

secure_store.notes: platform keystore; the only package that knows what a keychain is

flutter.notes:
The real boundary is the pubspec dependency graph, not the src/ directory. Dart does not prevent importing package:foo/src/x.dart — a lint discourages it. What actually stops messaging from using profile is that profile is not in messaging's pubspec, and a CI check that this graph matches this file. An AI adding the dependency to get its import to work fails that check.
No feature depends on another. They still reach each other — discovery opens a profile, a profile opens the composer — and apps/mobile owns that: a feature exposes routes and emits navigation intents, the shell wires them. That is why the shell is the only thing depending on everything.
Each feature is layered internally: domain (pure Dart) → application → data → presentation.
